rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise FM with LightGBM under a lambdarank objective, grouped into 6-row chunks to match the ~6-item evaluation lists, plus out-of-fold item/author rate features, will beat the 0.6016 baseline by a large margin.
rationale: Three mechanisms stack here. (1) The metric is a within-list ordering metric while the baseline optimises pointwise logloss, so a pairwise NDCG-weighted gradient aligns the training signal with the scored quantity. (2) Training groups of 43.5 rows impose a position discount and pair distribution nothing like the ~6-item valid lists; chunking to 6 makes the training lists the same shape as the scored lists. (3) The one genuinely new information source that varies WITHIN a user's list is item quality: a video's train-window long-view rate directly reorders that user's candidates, and 99.9% of valid videos appear in train so the encoding is populated. Trees can also exploit dur_bucket x item-rate interactions that a bilinear FM cannot.
expected_gain_derivation: Two additive parts. Structural part: [POINTWISE_BASELINE] plus [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]/[SHORT_EVAL_LISTS] — the organizers list loss change as unexplored [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] and a matched-length listwise gradient typically moves ranking metrics 0.02-0.03 when the current loss is pointwise. Feature part: item long-view rate is the strongest non-user-constant signal available and is not in base5 in aggregated form; [HIGH_COVERAGE] says it is almost always defined on valid, so I credit ~0.015-0.02. Sum ~0.045, well outside [SEED_NOISE] of 0.0008. Risk: item_agg is the block most exposed to the [MANDATORY DRIFT CHECK] and to [EXPOSURE_REGIME_CHANGE], which could zero the feature part.

block_justifications.item_agg: Video/author long-view and click rates vary across the rows of a single user's list, so unlike user-side aggregates they can actually reorder that list [WITHIN_USER_RANKING], and [HIGH_COVERAGE] means they are defined for 99.9% of valid rows.

hypothesis: Adding dur_feats (log duration and duration percentile rank within the user's list) to the LightGBM lambdarank/chunk-6 configuration will produce the first real gain, because the long_view label is mechanically a function of watch time against video length and duration varies strongly within a user's short list.
rationale: long_view on KuaiRand fires when play time crosses a threshold that is effectively relative to video length, so duration is the single strongest within-row driver of the label. base5 only sees a coarse dur_bucket categorical; log-duration gives the tree a continuous split axis, and the within-user percentile rank is an explicitly contrastive feature that encodes 'is this the longest or shortest item in THIS list', which is exactly the quantity a within-user ranker needs [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]. Percentile rank is also scale-free, so it survives the shift from 43-row train lists to 6-row valid lists better than raw duration does.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] lists duration-bias modelling as untouched, and [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD]/[ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD] show the static-field and capacity axes are exhausted, so the remaining headroom toward [CEILING] 0.8484 must come from label-mechanistic features. Iteration 1 changed model+objective+grouping+item_agg and moved only +0.0007, which tells me the structural axis is near-flat and the feature axis is where the effect must be; a duration term that directly drives the label plausibly buys an order of magnitude more than that, so ~+0.013, i.e. roughly a quarter of the gap the organizers' own failed feature experiments could not touch.

hypothesis: Adding cross_agg (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, and duration relative to the user's historically long-viewed duration) on top of the current frame, with the grouping tightened to 4-row chunks to match the valid median list length, will produce the first substantial gain because it is the only available block that is personalised AND varies within a user's list.
rationale: Every feature currently in the frame is either user-constant (user_id) or purely item-side (item_agg, duration). Item-side quality is already partly absorbed by exposure: the production policy only logs items it already thinks the user likes, so residual within-list order is driven by USER-SPECIFIC fit, not global item quality. cross_agg is exactly a user-specific fit signal computed from behaviour history (author/tag affinity, personal duration preference), which is the organizers' unexplored 'behaviour sequence' direction in the only form the action space exposes. Unlike cf, it is a direct history aggregate rather than a low-rank reconstruction of the exposure-biased interaction matrix, so it is far less likely to just re-encode the deployed recommender's own policy. Tightening group_chunk from 6 to 4 makes each training list closer to the median 4-row valid list, so the lambdarank position discount and truncation act over the same list geometry as the metric.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] names behaviour-based user features as untouched and [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]/[USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT] say only within-list-varying, user-specific quantities can move the score; cross_agg is the only such block left. Item-side item_agg was worth ~+0.0007 and dur_feats ~+0.0007 over the FM baseline, but those are non-personalised; a personalisation signal addresses a different and larger error component, and with [CEILING] 0.8484 vs current 0.6027 there is ample headroom. I discount from a naive +0.03 to +0.012 because [CF_DIAGNOSTIC_DIVERGENCE] warns that history-affinity signals can be anti-correlated with residual label on the exposure-biased standard log, which caps and could even invert the gain.
